mcq.q: According to the systematic meta-analysis of 49 randomized controlled trials (1,863 subjects), at what daily protein intake threshold do additional gains in muscle mass and strength plateau?
opts: 0.8 g/kg/day
~1.6 g/kg/day
2.5 g/kg/day
3.2 g/kg/day
mcq.rationale: The meta-analysis concluded that while protein supplementation enhances 1RM strength and fiber CSA, intakes exceeding ~1.6 g/kg of body weight per day do not further contribute to gains in muscle mass or strength.

mcq.q: What is the baseline U.S. Dietary Reference Intake (DRI) for dietary protein in adults over 18 years of age, regardless of physical activity status?
opts: 0.4 g/kg/day
0.8 g/kg/day
1.2 g/kg/day
1.7 g/kg/day
mcq.rationale: The standard U.S. DRI for protein is 0.8 g/kg/day, which is designed to prevent deficiency in sedentary populations, whereas resistance athletes require up to 1.6–1.7 g/kg/day.

mcq.q: What acute dose of high-quality protein consumed immediately post-exercise is recommended to maximally stimulate muscle protein synthesis in young individuals?
opts: 2 to 5 g
10 to 12 g
20 to 25 g
50 to 60 g
mcq.rationale: While 5–10 g can induce measurable synthesis, optimal post-exercise myofibrillar protein synthesis requires larger boluses on the order of 20 to 25 g of high-quality protein.

mcq.q: Which specific essential branched-chain amino acid serves as the primary chemical trigger for stimulating muscle protein synthesis via mTOR?
opts: Valine
Isoleucine
Leucine
Tryptophan
mcq.rationale: Leucine is the key essential amino acid that directly stimulates mTOR, acting as a molecular nutrient sensor that initiates messenger RNA translation.

mcq.q: What is the primary metabolic benefit of adding carbohydrates to a post-exercise protein beverage?
opts: It doubles the rate of muscle protein synthesis compared to protein alone
It aids in the resynthesis of depleted muscle glycogen stores
It permanently suppresses all cortisol secretion
It prevents amino acid transport into the kidneys
mcq.rationale: Co-ingesting carbohydrate does not markedly augment muscle protein synthesis beyond high-quality protein alone, but it is critical for replenishing muscle glycogen.

mcq.q: How long does the protein synthesis-stimulating effect of a single bolus of amino acids typically last in skeletal muscle?
opts: 10 to 15 minutes
1 to 2 hours
8 to 12 hours
24 to 48 hours
mcq.rationale: The acute stimulatory effect of a single dose of amino acids on muscle protein synthesis is transient, lasting approximately 1 to 2 hours.

mcq.q: Why is whey protein considered one of the most effective protein sources for stimulating muscle hypertrophy?
opts: It is rapidly digested and exceptionally rich in essential amino acids, especially leucine
It contains high concentrations of insoluble collagen fibers
It suppresses insulin secretion to facilitate lipid oxidation
It requires 8 to 10 hours for gastric emptying
mcq.rationale: Whey protein derived from milk is rapidly digested and contains high concentrations of essential amino acids and leucine, producing rapid hyperaminoacidemia.

mcq.q: How is the modern concept of the 'anabolic window of opportunity' best characterized?
opts: A strict 15-minute period immediately following the final repetition
A broad window extending from just before exercise to several hours post-exercise
A window that opens only after 24 hours of complete fasting
An anabolic phase that occurs exclusively during sleep
mcq.rationale: The window of opportunity lasts from just before the onset of resistance exercise to several hours post-exercise, allowing flexible nutrient timing.

ms.q: Which of the following outcomes were confirmed by the systematic meta-analysis of 49 randomized controlled trials regarding protein supplementation during resistance training? (Select all that apply)
opts: Significantly enhanced 1-repetition maximum (1RM) strength gains
Increased muscle fiber cross-sectional area (CSA)
Increased whole-muscle cross-sectional area
Linear, unlimited strength increases at intakes exceeding 3.5 g/kg/day
ms.rationale: The meta-analysis showed significant improvements in 1RM strength, fiber CSA, and whole-muscle CSA, but benefits plateaued at ~1.6 g/kg/day.

ms.q: Which practical dietary strategies optimize the skeletal muscle hypertrophic response to chronic resistance training? (Select all that apply)
opts: Consuming repeated moderate doses of protein throughout recovery rather than one large meal
Targeting a total daily intake between 1.6 and 1.7 g/kg of body weight
Ingesting 20 to 25 g of high-quality protein immediately post-exercise
Restricting all protein intake for 6 hours post-exercise to promote autophagy
ms.rationale: Repeated moderate protein boluses, daily intakes of 1.6–1.7 g/kg, and a 20–25 g post-exercise dose optimize 24-hour muscle protein synthesis.

ms.q: Which characteristics define an optimal protein source for maximizing muscle protein synthesis? (Select all that apply)
opts: Rapid digestion and absorption kinetics
High density of essential amino acids (EAAs)
High concentration of the branched-chain amino acid leucine
Absence of all nitrogenous compounds
ms.rationale: High-quality proteins are rapidly digested, rich in essential amino acids, and high in leucine, which together stimulate the mTOR pathway.

ms.q: What physiological benefits occur when carbohydrate is co-ingested with protein following a resistance training session? (Select all that apply)
opts: Aids in the replenishment and resynthesis of muscle glycogen stores
Stimulates pancreatic insulin secretion to create an anabolic hormonal environment
Substantially increases protein synthesis beyond protein alone
Supports recovery from glycogen-depleting resistance workouts
ms.rationale: Carbohydrates replenish muscle glycogen and stimulate insulin secretion, but do not markedly increase muscle protein synthesis beyond high-quality protein alone.

tf.q: Daily dietary protein intakes exceeding 1.6 g/kg of body weight provide continuous, linear increases in muscle size in resistance-trained athletes.
tf.feedback: False. Meta-analytic evidence confirms that muscle mass and strength gains plateau at ~1.6 g/kg/day; higher intakes yield no additional hypertrophy.

tf.q: A net positive protein balance occurs when skeletal muscle protein synthesis exceeds muscle protein breakdown.
tf.feedback: True. Muscle hypertrophy requires a net positive protein balance over time (synthesis > breakdown).

tf.q: The current U.S. Dietary Reference Intake (DRI) for protein is 1.7 g/kg/day for all adults.
tf.feedback: False. The U.S. DRI for adults over 18 years is 0.8 g/kg/day; 1.6 to 1.7 g/kg/day is the athletic recommendation for resistance training.

tf.q: Consuming protein before or during exercise can stimulate muscle protein synthesis during prolonged or repeated training sessions.
tf.feedback: True. Providing amino acids peri-workout maintains aminoacidemia and elevates protein synthesis during extended training bouts.

tf.q: The stimulatory effect of a single bolus of amino acids on muscle protein synthesis remains fully elevated for 24 hours.
tf.feedback: False. The synthetic response to a single dose of amino acids is transient, returning to baseline within 1 to 2 hours.

tf.q: Whey protein is particularly effective for muscle hypertrophy because it digests rapidly and is rich in leucine.
tf.feedback: True. Whey's rapid absorption kinetics and high leucine concentration trigger rapid mTOR activation.

tf.q: Co-ingesting carbohydrate with protein significantly multiplies the rate of muscle protein synthesis compared to protein alone.
tf.feedback: False. Adding carbohydrate does not markedly alter protein balance over protein alone, though it is essential for glycogen resynthesis.

tf.q: Ingesting repeated small-to-moderate doses of protein across the day can be more effective for hypertrophy than consuming one large daily protein meal.
tf.feedback: True. Repeated doses repeatedly restimulate muscle protein synthesis across a 24-hour period.

cloze.statement: In resistance-trained individuals, dietary protein intake beyond **~1.6 g/kg** of body weight per day does not further enhance muscle mass gains.
The baseline U.S. Dietary Reference Intake for sedentary adults over 18 years of age is **0.8 g/kg per day**.
To maximize muscle protein synthesis after resistance exercise, athletes should consume **20 to 25 g** of high-quality protein.
The branched-chain amino acid **leucine** serves as a potent chemical trigger for activating muscle protein synthesis.
Muscle hypertrophy requires a condition of **net positive protein balance** where synthesis exceeds breakdown.
The stimulatory effect of a single dose of amino acids on muscle protein synthesis is transient and lasts **1 to 2 h**.
Adding carbohydrate to post-exercise protein ingestion primarily aids in the resynthesis of **muscle glycogen**.
Athletes engaged in intensive resistance training may require daily protein intakes as high as **1.7 g/kg per day**.

sa.q: A collegiate strength athlete weighing 80 kg consumes 240 g of protein daily (3.0 g/kg/day) from supplements and claims this doubles his muscle protein synthesis compared to 1.6 g/kg/day. Based on clinical evidence, evaluate this claim and outline an evidence-based daily intake, acute post-exercise dose, and protein quality recommendation.
sa.model: The athlete's claim is physiologically and empirically incorrect. A systematic meta-analysis of 49 randomized controlled trials demonstrated that gains in 1RM strength and muscle fiber cross-sectional area plateau at ~1.6 g/kg/day, with no additional hypertrophic benefit observed at higher intakes. Consuming 3.0 g/kg/day simply leads to oxidation of excess amino acids into urea. For an 80 kg athlete, an evidence-based recommendation includes: 1) A daily intake of 1.6 to 1.7 g/kg/day (~128–136 g total protein), distributed across 3–5 meals; 2) An acute post-exercise bolus of 20 to 25 g of high-quality protein (such as whey protein, rich in essential amino acids and leucine) consumed during the peri-workout window; and 3) Inclusion of carbohydrate to replenish depleted muscle glycogen stores.
criteria: Refutes the 3.0 g/kg claim citing meta-analytic evidence that hypertrophy plateaus at ~1.6 g/kg/day.
Calculates or specifies an appropriate daily intake (1.6–1.7 g/kg/day, or ~128–136 g for an 80 kg individual).
Prescribes an acute post-exercise dose of 20–25 g of high-quality, leucine-rich protein (e.g., whey) and justifies carbohydrate co-ingestion for glycogen resynthesis.

mcq.q: Which master regulatory enzyme controls the rate of protein synthesis within skeletal myofibrils by integrating mechanical, hormonal, and amino acid cues?
opts: AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)
Mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR)
Glycogen synthase kinase-3
Lactate dehydrogenase
mcq.rationale: mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) is the master serine/threonine kinase that integrates upstream signals to control mRNA translation and protein synthesis.

mcq.q: What is the primary physiological stimulus that initiates the molecular signaling cascade activating mTOR in resistance-trained muscle?
opts: Cellular hypoxia
Mechanical stretch applied to the muscle
Glycogen depletion
Elevated blood lactate
mcq.rationale: The primary stimulus for muscle protein synthesis is the mechanical stretch and tension applied during resistance exercise, which activates mTOR via IGF-1 pathways.

mcq.q: What happens to skeletal muscle hypertrophy when mTOR is blocked experimentally using pharmaceutical inhibitors such as rapamycin?
opts: Hypertrophy occurs at twice the normal rate
Resistance exercise fails to produce muscle hypertrophy
Muscle fibers multiply via rapid hyperplasia
Skeletal muscle converts into adipose tissue
mcq.rationale: When mTOR is blocked experimentally, resistance exercise fails to produce muscle hypertrophy, proving that mTOR activation is an obligatory requirement for muscle growth.

mcq.q: Which hormone acts as a potent anabolic stimulus that enhances translational efficiency of mRNA in the presence of adequate amino acids?
opts: Glucagon
Insulin
Cortisol
Epinephrine
mcq.rationale: Insulin promotes the efficient translation of genetic codes carried by mRNA into functional proteins in the presence of adequate amino acid substrate.

mcq.q: What term describes the cellular process of synthesizing new ribosomes to expand the translational capacity of skeletal muscle fibers?
opts: Mitochondrial fission
Ribosome biogenesis
Sarcomere degradation
Autogenic inhibition
mcq.rationale: Ribosome biogenesis refers to the creation of new ribosomes, which increases total translational capacity and is essential for long-term hypertrophy.

mcq.q: What occurs to muscle fiber remodeling if the synthesis of new ribosomes is blocked biochemically during resistance overload?
opts: Muscles fail to undergo hypertrophy
Muscle protein synthesis increases tenfold
Fibers undergo longitudinal splitting
Endurance capacity increases by 300%
mcq.rationale: When the synthesis of new ribosomes is blocked biochemically, skeletal muscle fails to undergo hypertrophy despite mechanical overload.

mcq.q: In addition to controlling cytoplasmic translation, what critical nuclear role does mTOR perform in the muscle growth process?
opts: Regulating the synthesis of ribosomes in the cell nucleus
Breaking down sarcomeric Z-disks
Transporting glycogen into the bloodstream
Inhibiting satellite cell activation
mcq.rationale: Recent research confirms that mTOR localizes to the cell nucleus to coordinate the synthesis of ribosomes (ribosome biogenesis) in addition to regulating translation.

mcq.q: Why does ingesting leucine-rich protein during the peri-exercise window produce greater muscle hypertrophy than exercise alone?
opts: Leucine directly activates mTOR, adding a chemical stimulus to the mechanical tension stimulus
Leucine converts directly into testosterone in the bloodstream
Leucine inhibits all cellular protein degradation permanently
Leucine eliminates the need for ribosomal translation
mcq.rationale: Leucine acts as an intracellular nutrient signal that activates mTOR, synergizing with mechanical stretch to induce greater protein synthesis than exercise alone.

ms.q: Which upstream stimuli and nutrient signals directly activate the mTOR signaling complex in skeletal muscle? (Select all that apply)
opts: Mechanical stretch and tension
Insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1)
Intracellular amino acid availability, especially leucine
Severe prolonged intracellular ATP depletion
ms.rationale: Mechanical stretch, IGF-1, and amino acids (especially leucine) activate mTOR. Severe ATP depletion activates AMPK, which inhibits mTOR.

ms.q: Which cellular mechanisms explain how insulin promotes muscle hypertrophy in young skeletal muscle? (Select all that apply)
opts: Stimulates protein synthesis in the presence of adequate amino acid substrate
Promotes more efficient conversion of mRNA into proteins (translation)
Directly degrades existing actin and myosin filaments
Enhances amino acid uptake into the intracellular compartment
ms.rationale: Insulin stimulates protein synthesis, improves mRNA translation efficiency, and promotes amino acid uptake; it does not degrade myofibrillar proteins.

ms.q: Which statements correctly describe the role of ribosome biogenesis in skeletal muscle hypertrophy? (Select all that apply)
opts: It expands the muscle fiber's total translational capacity
It involves the synthesis of new ribosomes
Blocking ribosome synthesis prevents muscle hypertrophy
It is regulated in part by mTOR activity in the cell nucleus
ms.rationale: All four statements are correct: ribosome biogenesis creates new ribosomes to expand translational capacity, is nuclear-regulated by mTOR, and is required for hypertrophy.

ms.q: Which of the following events occur downstream of mTOR activation during resistance training recovery? (Select all that apply)
opts: Accelerated translation of mRNA transcripts into myofibrillar proteins
Increased synthesis of actin and myosin filaments
Complete shutdown of all cellular ribosome production
Coordination of nuclear ribosome biogenesis
ms.rationale: mTOR accelerates mRNA translation, drives actin and myosin synthesis, and coordinates nuclear ribosome biogenesis; it does not shut down ribosome production.

tf.q: mTOR controls the translation of messenger RNA (mRNA) into functional proteins within skeletal muscle myofibrils.
tf.feedback: True. mTOR is the primary kinase controlling the translational machinery converting mRNA into protein.

tf.q: If mTOR is blocked experimentally with inhibitors like rapamycin, resistance exercise still produces normal muscular hypertrophy.
tf.feedback: False. Experimental blockade of mTOR completely prevents resistance training-induced muscle hypertrophy.

tf.q: Mechanical stretch applied to muscle fibers activates mTOR via an intracellular pathway involving IGF-1.
tf.feedback: True. Mechanical strain triggers mechanotransduction signaling through IGF-1 to activate mTOR.

tf.q: Ribosomes are cellular organelles responsible for translating genetic codes carried by mRNA into proteins.
tf.feedback: True. Ribosomes execute translation, assembling amino acids into polypeptide chains based on mRNA templates.

tf.q: Increasing ribosome content in muscle fibers expands the translational capacity of the cell.
tf.feedback: True. More ribosomes provide greater translational machinery, allowing more protein to be synthesized simultaneously.

tf.q: Insulin can stimulate significant muscle protein synthesis even in the complete absence of intracellular amino acids.
tf.feedback: False. Insulin requires adequate amino acid substrate; in the absence of amino acids, it cannot stimulate protein synthesis.

tf.q: mTOR operates exclusively within the cytoplasm and has no role in the cell nucleus.
tf.feedback: False. Research demonstrates that mTOR localizes to the nucleus to coordinate ribosome biogenesis in addition to cytoplasmic translation.

tf.q: Leucine acts as an intracellular nutrient sensor that activates the mTOR signaling pathway.
tf.feedback: True. Leucine is sensed intracellularly to activate mTORC1 and stimulate myofibrillar protein synthesis.

cloze.statement: The rate of protein synthesis within myofibrils is controlled primarily by the kinase **mTOR**.
The primary mechanical stimulus for protein synthesis is **mechanical stretch** applied to the muscle.
Mechanical stretch activates mTOR through an intracellular signaling pathway involving **IGF-1**.
Organelles known as **ribosomes** execute the translation of mRNA transcripts into proteins.
The creation of new ribosomes to expand translational capacity is termed **ribosome biogenesis**.
In the presence of adequate substrate, the hormone **insulin** stimulates muscle protein synthesis and translation.
mTOR is involved in the synthesis of ribosomes in the **cell nucleus** in addition to regulating translation.
If the master kinase mTOR is blocked **experimentally**, resistance exercise fails to induce hypertrophy.

sa.q: Describe the central role of the master kinase mTOR in regulating skeletal muscle hypertrophy. Explain how mechanical tension and leucine converge on mTOR, and contrast translational efficiency with translational capacity (ribosome biogenesis).
sa.model: mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) serves as the master intracellular serine/threonine kinase coordinating myofibrillar protein synthesis. It integrates two primary upstream inputs: 1) Mechanical stretch, which triggers mechanotransductive signaling cascades via IGF-1 to activate mTOR; and 2) Chemical nutrient availability, where the essential amino acid leucine is sensed intracellularly to activate the mTOR complex. Once activated, mTOR controls the translation of mRNA into contractile proteins (actin and myosin). Translational efficiency refers to the speed and efficiency with which existing ribosomes translate mRNA transcripts into proteins, an acute process augmented by postprandial insulin surges. Translational capacity, by contrast, refers to the total number of ribosomes available in the muscle fiber. Through ribosome biogenesis—coordinated by nuclear mTOR activity—the cell synthesizes new ribosomes, expanding total protein-synthetic machinery. If either mTOR or ribosome biogenesis is blocked, muscle hypertrophy cannot occur.
criteria: Identifies mTOR as the master regulatory kinase integrating mechanical (stretch/IGF-1) and nutritional (leucine) inputs.
Explains how mechanical stretch and leucine converge to upregulate mRNA translation into myofibrillar proteins.
Contrasts translational efficiency (rate of mRNA processing by existing ribosomes) with translational capacity (ribosome biogenesis/number of ribosomes), noting nuclear mTOR involvement.

mcq.q: In the 2016 Netherlands study, how much greater was overnight myofibrillar protein synthesis in subjects who performed evening exercise with presleep protein (PRO+EX) compared to presleep protein alone (PRO)?
opts: ~5% greater
~15% greater
~35% greater
~100% greater
mcq.rationale: The 2016 Netherlands study demonstrated that overnight myofibrillar protein synthesis was ~35% greater in the PRO+EX group compared to the PRO-alone group.

mcq.q: What was the specific dose of labeled protein administered immediately before sleep to all subjects in the 2016 Netherlands study?
mcq.rationale: In the study protocol, each subject ingested an additional 30 g bolus of intrinsically labeled protein immediately before bed.

mcq.q: What did isotope tracer analysis reveal regarding the fate of dietary protein-derived amino acids in the PRO+EX subjects overnight?
opts: They were completely excreted in the urine without absorption
Significantly more labeled amino acids were incorporated into new myofibrils
They were converted entirely into adipose tissue
They caused acute gastrointestinal distress that halted protein synthesis
mcq.rationale: The PRO+EX group demonstrated significantly greater incorporation of labeled dietary amino acids directly into newly synthesized myofibrils overnight.

mcq.q: What type and duration of exercise did the PRO+EX cohort perform prior to receiving their post-workout and presleep protein drinks?
opts: 30 minutes of low-intensity cycling
60 minutes of lower-body resistance exercise
90 minutes of upper-body plyometrics
10 minutes of isometric core holds
mcq.rationale: The PRO+EX subjects completed a structured 60-minute lower-body resistance exercise bout following a standardized baseline meal.

mcq.q: Why is presleep protein ingestion an effective nutritional strategy for resistance-trained individuals?
opts: It increases overnight plasma amino acid availability and stimulates muscle protein synthesis during sleep
It permanently halts nocturnal growth hormone secretion
It converts slow-twitch fibers into fast-twitch fibers overnight
It eliminates the need for any daytime dietary protein
mcq.rationale: Presleep protein ingestion sustains plasma amino acid availability across the nocturnal fast, driving elevated muscle protein synthesis throughout sleep.

mcq.q: What acute dose of protein was consumed by all participants immediately after the 60-minute exercise or rest session, prior to the presleep drink?
opts: 5 g
mcq.rationale: Following the 60-minute exercise or rest period, all subjects consumed an immediate post-session beverage containing 20 g of protein.

mcq.q: What physiological consequence typically occurs during uninterrupted overnight sleep if no presleep protein is ingested?
opts: Protein synthesis exceeds breakdown by 500%
The body enters a prolonged fasting state where protein breakdown can exceed synthesis
Muscle glycogen stores double spontaneously
Satellite cells permanently fuse into tendons
mcq.rationale: During overnight sleep, the absence of exogenous amino acids creates a postabsorptive fasting state in which protein breakdown can exceed synthesis.

mcq.q: What did the Netherlands researchers conclude regarding the combination of evening resistance exercise and presleep protein ingestion?
opts: It causes severe muscle damage that impairs long-term recovery
It is an effective strategy to maximize skeletal muscle reconditioning overnight
It produces results identical to resting without food
It should be avoided due to interference with normal sleep stages
mcq.rationale: The researchers concluded that combining evening resistance exercise with presleep protein ingestion is a potent strategy to maximize overnight skeletal muscle reconditioning.

ms.q: Which methodological techniques were utilized in the 2016 Netherlands study to assess overnight muscle protein turnover? (Select all that apply)
opts: Continuous infusion of labeled amino acid isotopes
Pre- and post-sleep skeletal muscle biopsy collections
Repeated overnight blood sampling across 450 minutes of sleep
Underwater hydrostatic weighing every 30 minutes during sleep
ms.rationale: The study utilized labeled amino acid isotope infusions, pre/post-sleep muscle biopsies, and serial nocturnal blood sampling across 450 minutes.

ms.q: Which key findings were reported from the 2016 Netherlands presleep protein and evening exercise study? (Select all that apply)
opts: Overnight myofibrillar protein synthesis was ~35% greater in PRO+EX vs. PRO alone
Greater incorporation of dietary protein-derived amino acids into new myofibrils in PRO+EX
Exercise performed earlier in the evening increased the anabolic response to presleep protein
Presleep protein caused complete cessation of normal digestive enzyme activity
ms.rationale: The study showed ~35% higher overnight MPS, greater amino acid incorporation into myofibrils, and confirmed that prior exercise augments presleep protein utilization.

ms.q: Which factors explain why presleep protein supplementation enhances gains in muscle mass and strength over prolonged training? (Select all that apply)
opts: Maintains elevated plasma amino acid concentrations across an 8-hour nocturnal fast
Provides building blocks during peak periods of overnight hormonal recovery
Stimulates muscle protein synthesis during sleep
Replaces the requirement for mechanical tension during training
ms.rationale: Presleep protein sustains nocturnal aminoacidemia, provides substrate during recovery, and stimulates overnight MPS. It does not replace mechanical overload.

ms.q: In the Netherlands study, which characteristics applied to the subject cohort and standardized controls? (Select all that apply)
opts: 24 healthy young male subjects
Administration of a standardized dinner meal prior to testing
Equal 30 g presleep protein dose administered to both groups
Requirement that the PRO cohort run a marathon prior to sleeping
ms.rationale: The trial enrolled 24 healthy young men, provided a standardized dinner meal, and gave an identical 30 g presleep protein bolus to both cohorts.

tf.q: In the 2016 Netherlands study, performing evening resistance exercise increased overnight myofibrillar protein synthesis by ~35% compared to presleep protein alone.
tf.feedback: True. Overnight myofibrillar protein synthesis was ~35% greater in the PRO+EX cohort compared to PRO alone.

tf.q: Ingesting protein before sleep fails to stimulate muscle protein synthesis because the digestive tract shuts down during sleep.
tf.feedback: False. Ingested presleep protein is effectively digested and absorbed overnight, maintaining aminoacidemia and stimulating MPS.

tf.q: In the Netherlands study, both the exercise and resting groups received the same 30 g dose of labeled protein immediately before bed.
tf.feedback: True. Both groups consumed the identical 30 g labeled protein beverage immediately prior to sleep.

tf.q: Isotope tracer analysis showed that PRO+EX subjects incorporated fewer dietary amino acids into muscle tissue overnight than resting subjects.
tf.feedback: False. The PRO+EX subjects incorporated significantly more dietary-derived amino acids into newly synthesized myofibrils.

tf.q: Presleep protein supplementation has been demonstrated to increase strength and hypertrophy over prolonged resistance training programs.
tf.feedback: True. Chronic training studies confirm that presleep protein supplementation augments long-term gains in strength and muscle mass.

tf.q: Serial overnight blood draws were performed at intervals extending across 450 minutes of sleep in the Netherlands trial.
tf.feedback: True. Blood samples were drawn at 30, 60, 90, 150, 210, 330, and 450 minutes throughout sleep.

tf.q: Resistance exercise performed in the evening blunts the anabolic response to presleep protein ingestion.
tf.feedback: False. Evening resistance exercise enhances the muscle protein synthetic response to presleep protein ingestion.

tf.q: Combining evening resistance exercise with presleep protein ingestion is a practical strategy to maximize overnight muscle reconditioning.
tf.feedback: True. The study authors concluded this combination is highly effective for maximizing overnight recovery and hypertrophy.

Subjects in the Netherlands trial consumed an acute bolus of **30 g** of labeled protein immediately before sleep.

Overnight blood sampling in the study was conducted across **450 min** while the subjects slept.

sa.q: Analyze the methodology, isotope findings, and clinical outcomes of the 2016 Netherlands presleep resistance exercise study. Explain why combining evening resistance exercise with presleep protein ingestion provides a superior overnight anabolic environment compared to presleep protein ingestion alone.
sa.model: The 2016 Netherlands study investigated whether an acute evening resistance exercise bout enhances the overnight muscle protein synthesis (MPS) response to presleep protein ingestion. Twenty-four healthy young men were randomized to presleep protein alone (PRO) or evening exercise plus presleep protein (PRO+EX). Following a standardized meal, the PRO+EX cohort performed 60 minutes of lower-body resistance exercise while the PRO cohort rested. Both groups consumed a 20 g protein drink post-session, followed by continuous labeled amino acid isotope infusions, serial nocturnal blood sampling across 450 minutes of sleep, and pre/post-sleep muscle biopsies. Just prior to sleep, all subjects ingested a 30 g bolus of labeled protein. The findings demonstrated that overnight myofibrillar MPS was ~35% greater in the PRO+EX group compared to PRO alone. Furthermore, tracer analysis revealed significantly higher incorporation of dietary protein-derived amino acids into newly synthesized myofibrils in the exercised muscle. This demonstrates that prior resistance exercise sensitizes skeletal muscle to hyperaminoacidemia, directing circulating amino acids into contractile protein accretion and mitigating nocturnal fasting catabolism.
criteria: Summarizes study design: 24 young men, standardized meal, 60 min lower-body exercise vs. rest, 20 g post-session protein, and 30 g labeled presleep protein.
Identifies isotopic methods (continuous tracer infusion, 450 min serial blood sampling, pre/post-sleep muscle biopsies).

Reports core findings (~35% greater overnight myofibrillar MPS and greater dietary amino acid incorporation in PRO+EX) and explains the physiological rationale (exercise sensitizes muscle to utilize nocturnal amino acids).
